newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET - Rixon looks to perfect Turner approach.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Rixon looks to perfect Turner approach.

text.p: SHARJAH, Nov 5 - New Zealand coach Steve Rixon wants to perfect the brand of one-day cricket promoted by his ousted predecessor Glenn Turner, NZPA reported on Tuesday.

Rixon sees a lot of merit in the style of play developed by Turner last season, but the former Australian wicketkeeper believes the dumped coach's attacking theories on the limited overs game need adjusting to encourage the players to show more flexibility in their approach.
Rixon's new regime goes under the spotlight here in the Champions Trophy tournament when New Zealand play world champions Sri Lanka and Pakistan.
The Kiwis arrived in the United Arab Emirates late last night, and open their account on Thursday when they take on Sri Lanka.
Rixon believes this tournament will offer his team an ideal forum in which to develop their limited overs philosophy.

Turner's mandate called for all-out attack from his batsmen. It led to some wonderful displays of power hitting, but the side were also at times most vulnerable because they refused to adapt their game if a couple of early wickets fell.
Last summer the Kiwis looked to score at least 90 runs from the opening 15 overs, but Rixon thinks their sights should be lowered during the important, early stages of the innings.
"The general philosophy adopted last season will stay, there's nothing wrong with it," Rixon told NZPA.
"The boys are quite happy with the way they play the one-day game, but I think a more realistic target from the first 15 overs is 75. That's five runs an over which is good going," he said.
"That leads towards a possible 250-plus score which should see you win 80 percent of your matches."
"A sign of the attacking brand of cricket we play this year will be the flexibility we use.
"It'll be a more educated version of what's gone on before," he said.
"I want them to feel they can bat normally without having to chase things that are wide, and basically throwing their wickets away."

Rixon doesn't expect that he and fellow tour selectors -- captain Lee Germon and senior batsman Mark Greatbatch -- will decide on their playing 11 for the opening match on Thursday until the morning of the game.
However, he suggested a varied bowling attack was needed.
"We have a lot of options open to us in our style of bowling. I don't like the idea of using four bowlers of the same type in a one-day game," Rixon said.
The New Zealanders of l995-96 placed a lot of faith in the medium pacers plus offspinner Dipak Patel, with seamers Danny Morrison, Chris Cairns and Dion Nash playing bit parts.
That seems likely to change.

The Kiwis will spend a lot of time before Thursday's match viewing videotapes of the Sri Lankans in action. What they glean from that, plus the ground conditions at Sharjah Stadium, will determine how they set about countering the rollicking Sri Lankan batsmen.
Injuries have already affected the New Zealanders, with spinners Patel and Mark Haslam carrying injuries on their arrival here.
The Kiwi touring party has been boosted to 16 in number, with the 11th hour inclusion of Otago offspinner Paul Wiseman, who is here to act as cover for Patel and Haslam.
